newsitem.title: USA: Motorola to quit making hand-held PDAs.
newsitem.headline: Motorola to quit making hand-held PDAs.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Wednesday it plans to quit producing its personal digital assistants (PDA), a hand-held computer that comprised only a small portion of the technology giant's business.

"It's true we will no longer be producing Marco and the Envoy (PDA) products, but we will still provide wireless communications support for PDA platforms via our Personal Personal Messenger product," said a spokeswoman for Motorola's Wireless Data Group, which manufactures the devices.
Asked if the company would take a charge in relation to the plan, she said there was "nothing material to disclose".
The spokeswoman said the PDA products, which use a pen rather than a keyboard, will be taken off the price list at the end of the year. But the company will continue to sell current inventories.
The devices, which allowed users to write handwritten memos and email messages, sold for about $1,000 each. They could be connected to a computer at home or the office.
"On a revenue basis it would be very insignificant," an analyst, who asked not to be named, said of Motorola's move to discontinue the PDA products.
The Motorola spokeswoman declined to give details on revenues for the PDA line.
"There really hasn't been much of a catalyst to owning them (PDA products) since laptops have come down in size and weight, and have more capability," the analyst said.

The Personal Messenger product, which Motorola will continue to make and market, is a card that plugs into notebook computers and other manufacturers' PDA products, for example Apple Computer Inc's Apple Newton.
